ar.title: أقراص كشك ناشف للتخزين
ar.intro: تُحفظ أقراص الكشك شهوراً. وعند نقعها وطهيها في المرقة تصبح صلصة الكشك التي تُقدَّم باردة مع البصل المحمر.

steps.n2: أضف الدقيق المنخول تدريجياً واعجن حتى تحصل على عجينة كثيفة لا تلتصق بالوعاء.
steps.n3: اتركها تتخمر 4–5 أيام، مع رش الدقيق على وجهها.
steps.n4: شكّلها أقراصاً صغيرة مستديرة ومسطحة، وجفّفها في الهواء الطلق بضعة أيام مع تقليب كل قرص مرتين يومياً حتى تصبح صلبة جداً.
steps.n5: خزّنها في علبة محكمة الغلق، أقراصاً أو مدقوقة بودرة، جاهزة لطهي الكشك.
steps.n6: بالزبادي (الوصفة 345 في الكتاب): حضّرها بنفس الطريقة باستخدام الزبادي بدلاً من اللبن. ولأن الزبادي متخمر أصلاً فهو يحتاج 2–3 أيام فقط، وطعمه مختلف تماماً.
steps.n7: الكشك الصعيدي (الوصفة 346 في الكتاب): اشطف برغلاً ناعماً وافرده ليجف، ثم غطّه بلبن رائب مملح في زلعة فخار كبيرة 5 أيام، مع إضافة مزيد من اللبن الرائب كل 24 ساعة. في اليوم السادس اعجنه عجينة متماسكة، وشكّله أقراصاً صغيرة مستديرة وجفّفها بنفس الطريقة.

en.title: Dried Kishk Cakes for Storing (Kishk li-l-Takhzin)
en.intro: Recipe 344, page 150 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

steps.n1: Dissolve the salt in the milk.
steps.n2: Gradually work in the sifted flour until you have a thick dough that comes cleanly away from the bowl.
steps.n3: Leave it to ferment for 4–5 days, sprinkling flour over the top.
steps.n4: Shape it into small, flat round cakes and dry them in the open air for a few days, turning each cake twice a day, until very hard.
steps.n5: Store in a tightly closed box, as cakes or pounded to a powder, ready to cook into kishk.
steps.n6: With yogurt (recipe 345 in the book): make it the same way with yogurt instead of milk. As yogurt is already fermented it needs only 2–3 days, and the taste is quite different.
steps.n7: Upper Egyptian kishk (recipe 346 in the book): rinse fine bulgur and spread it to dry, then cover it with salted soured milk in a large earthenware pot for 5 days, adding more soured milk every 24 hours. On the sixth day knead it into a stiff dough, shape small round cakes and dry them the same way.

legacySteps: Dissolve the salt in the milk.
Gradually work in the sifted flour until you have a thick dough that comes cleanly away from the bowl.
Leave it to ferment for 4–5 days, sprinkling flour over the top.
Shape it into small, flat round cakes and dry them in the open air for a few days, turning each cake twice a day, until very hard.
Store in a tightly closed box, as cakes or pounded to a powder, ready to cook into kishk.
With yogurt (recipe 345 in the book): make it the same way with yogurt instead of milk. As yogurt is already fermented it needs only 2–3 days, and the taste is quite different.

Upper Egyptian kishk (recipe 346 in the book): rinse fine bulgur and spread it to dry, then cover it with salted soured milk in a large earthenware pot for 5 days, adding more soured milk every 24 hours. On the sixth day knead it into a stiff dough, shape small round cakes and dry them the same way.
